source.title: The Vocabulary Is Already Here: Adapting Pretrained Interpretable Features for Generative Recommendation
source.authors: Ziluowen Luo; Ruo-Chen Liu; Jun Yin; Hao Yan; Zheng Hu; Xin-Ze Shi; Chao-Zhuo Li; Cheng-Qi Zhang; Sen-Zhang Wang

page_placements.theme: Conditional behavioral control through dictionary features

record.tranche_reason: The study measures semantic alignment for selected SAE features in GPT-2-small using title-match rates and lift, a different measure bearing narrowly on whether SAE features capture interpretable semantic patterns. It does not test superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The study uses pretrained SAE features as recommendation tokens but does not measure overlapping directions, capacity pressure, neuron polysemanticity, or feature dimensionality. PID collision rates concern item token sequences, not overlap among neural feature directions. The reported activation steering is deliberately induced and concerns recommendation retrieval, not naturally occurring superposition.
record.test_reason: The study uses a pretrained GPT-2-small SAE (gpt2-small-res-jb) as a token vocabulary for generative recommendation and reports its own method's performance. The semantic results are three hand-picked feature examples (f4260, f14730, f13542) illustrating explainability. Title-match rates are computed only on items whose PIDs, chosen by the authors' activation-IDF selection, contain the feature. No version is tested: there is no measure of superposition geometry, capacity pressure, polysemanticity, feature spread across neurons, SAE recovery or reconstruction quality, completeness, stability, or dimensionality. The steering result (r4) is a deliberately induced retrieval effect in the authors' recommender, not a property of the LLM's representation.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that a pretrained SAE dictionary can be adapted, without vocabulary fitting, into a shared, interpretable item vocabulary. Via PIDs and SPA, this gives competitive generative recommendation and traceable retrieval explanations. They leave more general-purpose interpretable vocabularies to future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies a pretrained SAE dictionary to recommendation item descriptions and retrieval; it does not reproduce the original superposition method or measure its geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The induced retrieval response varies across features and steering doses; Toys results are reported as a mean over features.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected pretrained GPT-2-small SAE features, when chosen as item tokens by activation-IDF selection, align strongly with lexical title patterns. Examples: f4260 at 98.7% agreement and 7.91× lift; brushes at 92.4% and 18.31×; LEGO at 99.6% and 13.77×.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretrained SAE features transfer as human-interpretable semantic units to out-of-domain product text (an SAE interpretability/transfer claim, not superposition).

fits_no_version.finding: Editing history activations of SAE feature f4260 by +0.50 raises target-feature exposure@10 by 1.365 pp versus matched controls (nominal CI [0.652, 2.189], 332 users).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation edits to SAE-feature tokens can causally steer feature-specific retrieval in SAE-tokenized recommenders.

record.problems: The semantic evidence is limited to selected features and lexical title-match proxies; the study does not report a broad feature-recovery or reconstruction evaluation for the claim. The uncertainty interval reported for steering is nominal and uncorrected across 36 feature–direction comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were included: recommendation performance, PID collisions, content-neighborhood overlap, tokenization timing, and recommendation steering metrics do not measure the representational geometry or the tested semantic feature-alignment measure.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity transitions or geometry.
All: no capacity or neuron polysemanticity analysis.
Feature spread across neurons and SAE recovery or reconstruction quality. Feature interpretability is shown only for three selected examples, as a tool demonstration.
Completeness, stability, canonicity of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: This is a recommendation-systems paper that treats SAE interpretability as a premise. The reader's V4 'tests' / T2 assignment and its supports/limits_scope labels are removed: the semantic evidence is cherry-picked illustration on method-selected items, not a test of whether LLMs contain SAE-recoverable sparse features. Other results (recall/NDCG, collision rates, Overlap@20, tokenization time) concern the recommender and do not bear on any version.

versions.untested_parts: Sparse-feature superposition, near-orthogonal overlapping directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether feature competition for capacity causes polysemantic neurons or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
The study reports semantic-match evidence for selected SAE features in GPT-2-small, but does not test feature spread across neurons, reconstruction or recovery quality, or generality across LLMs.
The study uses SAE indices as recommendation vocabulary but does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical representational units.
The study does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: GPT-2-small with Bloom's SAE (gpt2-small-res-jb)
rows.operation_detail: Measured title-rule agreement among training items whose PID contains feature f4260.
rows.measure: Title agreement with the hunting-and-shooting lexical rule; lift over training-catalog prevalence
rows.note: Feature descriptions are external automatically generated descriptions; the study says they were not used as model inputs.
rows.check: This is an illustrative, author-selected feature whose agreement is measured on items selected by the study's own PID policy, so it is a selection-conditioned value. Interpretability of one feature does not measure whether the LLM stores features in superposition or whether an SAE recovers them. The value and the ≈12.5% baseline are read correctly.

rows.subject: GPT-2-small with Bloom's SAE (gpt2-small-res-jb)
rows.operation_detail: Measured title agreement for items containing the feature.
rows.note: Reported as an additional semantic example; item count is not stated.
rows.check: This is an author-selected illustrative example (Appendix D) computed on PID-selected items. It does not measure any version. The item count and baseline prevalence are not stated.

rows.subject: GPT-2-small with Bloom's SAE (gpt2-small-res-jb)
rows.operation_detail: Measured title agreement for items containing the feature.
rows.note: Reported as an additional semantic example; item count is not stated.
rows.check: This is an author-selected illustrative example computed on PID-selected items, and it does not measure any version. The item count is stated in Figure 6 (544/546 at K=4), contrary to the record's note. Figure 6 also gives K=16/32 as 626/628, though it prints 93.7% (likely a typo for 99.7%).

rows.subject: T5-PR Full SPA
rows.operation_detail: Edited existing history activations for a feature while keeping model parameters and candidate PIDs fixed; compared with matched control edits.
rows.measure: Target-feature exposure@10 change relative to matched control edits
rows.note: This is a deliberately induced retrieval response, not evidence that the behavior occurs without activation editing.
rows.check: This is an induced activation edit inside the authors' recommender measuring retrieval exposure, not a representational property of the model. It is also nominal, uncorrected across 36 comparisons, and is one of six features tested per domain.

relation.reason: Uses pretrained interpretable features as a recommendation vocabulary without testing their superposition, capacity explanation, completeness, stability, canonicality, or dimensionality.

tranche.reason: Reuses a frozen pretrained SAE dictionary for recommendation and evaluates tokenization, retrieval, and induced steering; these do not test the listed superposition claims.

source_check.notes: Appendix C.2 confirms all r4 conditions and numbers. Its interval uses 500 paired user-bootstrap resamples without correction across 36 feature–direction comparisons; the induced retrieval response does not establish a superposition claim.
